mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 2-month acceleration in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) above the prior 6-month average signals stronger household demand, which raises earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth > 0.3% monthly for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or Rank IC falls below 0.05 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month rise in the unemployment rate above 4.0% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which pressure corporate margins and lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or Rank IC drops below 0.04 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A 2-month contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below 1.0% signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings growth and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or Rank IC falls below 0.04 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month rise in the federal funds rate above 5.0% signals a tightening monetary cycle that raises discount rates and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or Rank IC drops below 0.04 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A 2-month decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) below the prior 6-month average signals weaker household demand, which reduces earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth < -0.2% monthly for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or Rank IC falls below 0.04 over any 3-year window.

failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or Rank IC drops below 0.04 over any 3-year window.
